page.layout: One page of text in verse, no margin notes. Epigrams set in full lines, each with a small italic rubric above it. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.head: In eundem Alexandrum:
main_text.p: Mirum si vomuit nigrum post fata cruorem Borgia quem biberat, concoquere haud potuit.
main_text.head: Aliud in eundem:
main_text.p: Sub quo bella diu viguerunt, pestis in urbe, Diluvium populo, semper amara fames: Mille hominum caedes, & furta incesta fuerunt: Causa mali tanti proditor ipse fuit.
Sacrilegus praedo, sacra qui venalia cunsta Fecerat, & tumquo polluit omne nephas.
main_text.head: Aliud in eundem:
main_text.p: Visuram se iterum Sixtum cum Roma putaret, Pro Sixto Sextum vidit, & ingemuit.
main_text.head: Aliud in eundem:
main_text.p: Bello, inimicitiis, furtisq; & caedibus baustam Italiam cernis Sexte, & obire potes?
main_text.head: Aliud in eundem:
main_text.p: Dic, in amicitiam coeant, & foedera iungant Mortales: dixit Sextus, & occubuit.
main_text.head: Aliud in eundem:
main_text.p: Piscatorem hominum ne te non Sexte putemus, Piscaris natum retibus ecce tuum.
main_text.head: Aliud in eundem:
main_text.p: Europam Tyrio quondam sedisse iuvenco Quis negat? Hspano[?] Iulia vecta bove est.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the first word of the opening line and "Hspano" in the last epigram, where the letter after H is unclear. "abiiacet" is also uncertain. "cunsta" and "baustam" are copied as printed; the letters are not fully clear in the scan. The faint text along the right margin is show-through and is not transcribed.
